Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Swanmore College. I am proud that Swanmore College is a happy place where pupils, teachers and support staff enjoy working together. I want Swanmore to be referred to as a ‘Centre of Excellence’ in all that we do. A place where excellent teaching and learning is observed, where exemplary behaviour and care is guaranteed, where excellent GCSE results are attained and opportunities for all to achieve and flourish is a given.
I want to see all pupils emerge from the college with a wide range of knowledge and experience, a group of lifelong friends, and a variety of interests that will continue to excite them in the years ahead. This will be achieved by working in partnership with parents, teachers, governors and the local community.
Should you wish to view the college or have any concerns regarding your child, please contact the College. I can assure you we will work together to answer any questions or concerns you may have.
Mr Jonathan Headteacher

Enrichment
This academic year we asked pupils for five possible Enrichment activity choices. Statement of Intent
At Swanmore College, Careers and PSHE work together to support pupils’ personal development, wellbeing and future destinations.
We are committed to ensuring that all pupils receive high-quality, impartial Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG). This enables young people to understand their strengths and interests, explore a wide range of opportunities, and make informed decisions at key transition points.
Our Careers programme is delivered through the curriculum, PSHE, careers education, employer and provider encounters, enrichment activities and personalised guidance. It is structured in line with national frameworks, including the Gatsby Benchmarks and the Careers Development Institute (CDI) framework, to ensure progression and consistency across Years 7–11.
We aim to prepare pupils for further education, training and employment, including academic, technical and vocational pathways. Parents and carers are valued as key partners and are supported with clear information and trusted signposting to help young people progress confidently into their next steps.

Gatsby Benchmarks: what are they?
A stable careers programme
Every school and college should have an embedded programme of career education and guidance that is known and understood by pupils, parents, teachers and employers.
Learning from career and labour market information
Every school and college should have an embedded programme of career education and guidance that is known and understood by pupils, parents, teachers and employers.
Addressing the needs of each pupil
Pupils have different career guidance needs. Opportunities for advice and support need to be tailored to the needs of each pupil. A school’s programme should embed equality and diversity considerations throughout.
Linking curriculum learning to careers
All teachers should link curriculum learning with careers, even if they are not subject teachers. This includes providing a range of examples of how the subject relates to future career paths.
Encounters with employers and employees
Every pupil should have multiple opportunities to learn from employers about work, employment and the skills that are valued in the workplace. This can be through a range of enrichment activities including visiting speakers, mentoring and enterprise schemes.
Experiences of workplaces
Every pupil should have first-hand experiences of the workplace through work visits, work shadowing and/or work experience to help their exploration of career opportunities, and expand their networks.
Encounters with further and higher education
All pupils should understand the full range of learning opportunities that are available to them. This includes academic and vocational routes and learning in schools, colleges, universities and in the workplace.
Every pupil should have opportunities for guidance interviews with a career adviser, who could be internal (a member of school staff) or external, provided they are trained to an appropriate level. These should be available whenever significant study or career choices are being made. All pupils should have individual needs addressed.

Prospectus
Welcome to Swanmore College
Thank you for taking the time to learn more about Swanmore College.
Choosing the right secondary school is one of the most important decisions a family can make. As you explore this prospectus, I hope you gain a sense of what makes Swanmore such a special place to learn, grow and belong.
Our vision is simple: Together We Thrive
This vision reflects our belief that every young person deserves to be known, valued and challenged to achieve their very best. We are committed to creating a culture where every pupil feels a strong sense of belonging, develops confidence and character, and achieves success through high expectations, support and opportunity.
At Swanmore, thriving means more than academic success alone. It means developing the knowledge, skills and experiences that enable young people to flourish both in school and beyond. Through an ambitious curriculum, rich extra-curricular opportunities and strong pastoral care, we encourage every pupil to discover new interests, develop their talents and contribute positively to our community.
Our vision is built on four simple principles:
These principles shape everything we do. They underpin our commitment to high standards, positive relationships and a culture where achievement, effort and kindness are valued equally.
We are proud of our school and of the opportunities it provides for young people to grow into confident, compassionate and successful individuals. Most importantly, we are proud of the community we build together with our pupils, families and staff.
We look forward to working in partnership with you to ensure your child thrives, both academically and personally, throughout their time at Swanmore College.

Why Choose Swanmore?
Families choose Swanmore because they want more than simply strong examination results.
They want a school where their child is known and valued.
They want a school where pupils feel safe, supported and encouraged to thrive.
They want a school that develops confidence, resilience and character alongside academic achievement.
They want opportunities that help young people discover new interests, build lasting friendships and create memories that stay with them long after they leave school.
At Swanmore College, we combine academic ambition with exceptional pastoral support, a broad and engaging curriculum, outstanding opportunities beyond the classroom and a genuine commitment to helping every child flourish.
Our pupils are encouraged to participate fully in school life. They are challenged to think deeply, work hard and take pride in their achievements. They are given opportunities to lead, contribute and make a difference. Most importantly, they are supported by staff who genuinely care about their success and wellbeing.
The result is a vibrant and inclusive community where pupils feel a strong sense of belonging and where families know their child is receiving an education that prepares them for their next stage of life, and beyond.
Our Curriculum: Learning that Inspires
At Swanmore College, we believe that every child deserves an education that helps them thrive.
Our curriculum sits at the heart of everything we do. It is designed not only to help pupils achieve academic success, but also to develop the confidence, character and life skills needed for the future.
The Swanmore Curriculum is built around four interconnected elements that shape each pupil's journey from Year 7 to Year 11:
Academic
A broad, ambitious and knowledge-rich curriculum that provides pupils with the skills and qualifications needed for future success.
Development
Opportunities to build confidence, resilience, wellbeing and the personal skills needed to become healthy, responsible and independent young adults.
Enrichment
Experiences beyond the classroom that encourage pupils to discover new interests, develop talents and experience success in different ways.
Destinations
Careers education, guidance and experiences that help pupils understand their options, raise aspirations and prepare for their next steps after Swanmore.
Together, these four elements ensure that pupils leave Swanmore with strong academic foundations, memorable experiences, a clear sense of who they are and the confidence to thrive in whatever path they choose next.
Academic Excellence
High expectations are central to life at Swanmore College.
We believe that every pupil can achieve great things when they are supported, challenged and inspired. Our classrooms are places where learning is valued, effort is celebrated and pupils are encouraged to take pride in their achievements.
Our teachers are passionate subject specialists who work hard to ensure lessons are engaging, ambitious and accessible to all learners. They combine expertise with a genuine commitment to helping pupils succeed.
Pupils are encouraged to ask questions, think critically, solve problems and develop independence in their learning. They learn that success comes through perseverance, resilience and a willingness to embrace challenge.
We are proud of the academic progress our pupils make and of the culture of ambition that exists throughout the College. Whether a pupil arrives with a clear vision of their future or is still discovering their strengths and interests, our aim is the same: to help them achieve their very best and leave Swanmore ready for the next stage of their journey.
Building Strong Foundations: Core subjects explained
English, Mathematics and Science form the foundation of every pupil's education at Swanmore College. As the core GCSE subjects studied by all pupils, they provide the essential knowledge, skills and confidence needed for success across the curriculum and beyond.
These subjects play a vital role in preparing young people for further education, employment and adult life. Through inspiring teaching, high expectations and carefully planned learning, pupils develop the literacy, numeracy and scientific understanding that underpin future success.
Across all three subjects, our dedicated teachers combine expert knowledge with high expectations and strong support, helping pupils make excellent progress and develop a genuine love of learning.
By building strong foundations in English, Mathematics and Science, we equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to thrive at Swanmore College and beyond.
Creativity and Expression
Creativity plays an important role in helping young people discover who they are and what they can achieve.
At Swanmore College, pupils have opportunities to explore their talents through art, music, photography, drama and a wide range of creative subjects.
Creative subjects encourage imagination, resilience and self-expression while helping pupils build confidence and develop new skills.
Whether performing on stage, creating artwork, learning an instrument or sharing their ideas through another medium, pupils are encouraged to take pride in their creativity and celebrate their individuality.
Practical Learning for Life
Education should prepare young people for life beyond the classroom.
Our practical subjects provide opportunities for pupils to develop valuable real-world skills through hands-on learning experiences.
From designing and creating products in Design Technology to developing independence and healthy living skills through Food and Nutrition, pupils are encouraged to solve problems, think creatively and apply their learning in meaningful ways.
These experiences help pupils develop confidence, resilience and a sense of achievement that extends far beyond the classroom.
Sport and Physical Wellbeing
Sport is an important part of life at Swanmore College and contributes significantly to the wellbeing, confidence and personal development of our pupils.
Whether competing at a high level, representing the College in fixtures or participating for enjoyment and fitness, pupils are encouraged to be active and involved.
Pupils can participate in a wide range of sports including football, rugby, netball, cricket, athletics, badminton, tennis and many others.
Sport teaches far more than physical skills. Through training, competition and teamwork, pupils develop resilience, determination, leadership and self-confidence. They learn how to support one another, overcome setbacks and celebrate success.
We are proud of the sporting opportunities available to our pupils and of the positive role that sport plays in helping young people develop healthy, active lifestyles.

Set within a welcoming and attractive environment, Swanmore College provides facilities that support learning, creativity and personal development.

Our campus combines specialist teaching spaces, sports facilities and outdoor areas that help create a positive atmosphere where pupils feel safe, supported and inspired.
The College environment reflects our commitment to providing the very best opportunities for every pupil while fostering a strong sense of community and belonging.

Beyond the Classroom
Some of the most memorable experiences of school life happen beyond lessons.
At Swanmore College, learning extends far beyond the classroom through a rich programme of enrichment activities, leadership opportunities, educational visits and residential experiences. These opportunities help pupils build confidence, develop independence and create lasting memories while bringing their learning to life.
Pupils can take part in a wide variety of activities including sport, performing arts, pupil leadership, Duke of Edinburgh's Award, Arts Award, journalism through Swan Life Press and a broad range of clubs and enrichment opportunities.
Educational visits play an important role in the Swanmore experience. From local fieldwork and curriculum visits to national and international trips, pupils have opportunities to deepen their understanding of subjects through real-world experiences. Recent and regular opportunities include the biennial Iceland trip, Belgium Battlefields visit, ski trips, theatre trips and museum visits. These visits help pupils develop independence, resilience and a broader understanding of the world around them.
Rights, Responsibility And Community
We are proud of the positive culture that exists throughout our College community.
As a UNICEF Rights Respecting Gold School, we are committed to promoting respect, equality and inclusion. Pupils are encouraged to understand their rights, value the perspectives of others and contribute positively to society.
Our commitment to sustainability, community engagement and social responsibility helps pupils develop into thoughtful and responsible citizens who are prepared to make a difference in the world around them.
Pupil Leadership
We believe that young people should play an active role in shaping their school community.
There are many opportunities for pupils to take on leadership roles and contribute positively to College life. From the election of a Head Girl and Head Boy each year to serving as prefects or members of the School Council, pupils are encouraged to represent their peers, develop leadership skills and play an active role in shaping the College community.
Our commitment to pupil voice is reflected throughout the College. We listen carefully to pupils' views and actively encourage them to share their ideas and perspectives.
Swan Life Press
Many of the photographs on this prospectus page have been taken by pupils as part of Swan Life Press, our pupil-led communications enrichment group.
Through Swan Life Press, pupils help to capture and share the life of the College from their own perspective. Their photographs offer a pupil’s-eye view of Swanmore, showing the moments, opportunities and experiences that matter to them.
Swan Life Press is also one of the ways pupils can contribute to the wider voice of the College, helping to celebrate achievements, share stories and reflect what it means to be part of the Swanmore community.
Wellbeing, Inclusion and SEND
At Swanmore College, we believe pupils achieve their best when they feel safe, supported and valued. Pastoral care is at the heart of our community, helping every young person develop confidence, resilience and a strong sense of belonging.
Our pastoral teams work closely with pupils and families to provide guidance, support and early intervention when needed. This may include emotional wellbeing support, attendance guidance, safeguarding support, peer mentoring, personal development programmes and individual pastoral care.

Smartphone-Free College Community
From September 2026, Swanmore College will become a smartphone-free environment.
This supports our commitment to creating a calm, focused environment where pupils can fully engage with their learning, connect face-to-face with peers, and make the most of daily life at the College.
Key Details for Families
Effective Date: 01 September 2026.
Permitted Devices: Simple feature phones (often called 'brick' phones) that can only make basic calls and send text messages.
Smartphones and Internet Devices: Not permitted on the College site.
We appreciate the support of our parents and carers as we work together to maintain a purposeful, disruption-free learning community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Swanmore School - Sports Day 2026: Attenborough Crowned House Champions!
pageCache.text:
Sports Day 2026: Attenborough Crowned House Champions!
The final scores are in, and we can now reveal the overall winners of our House Championship!
Following a year of friendly competition, teamwork and determination, the House Championship has come to an exciting conclusion.
The overall results combine points earned across our inter-house PE tournaments with performances on Sports Day, where pupils gave their all in a wide range of events. From football, rounders and capture the flag to netball, dodgeball, tug of war and the athletics events, every point counted. Bonus points were also awarded for outstanding house attendance on Sports Day, making every pupil's contribution even more important.
A huge well done to everyone who took part, supported their housemates and demonstrated fantastic team spirit throughout the year.
Final House Championship Standings:
🥇 1 – Attenborough: 848 points 🥈 2 – Whittle: 815 points 🥉 3 – Hawking: 728 points 4 – MacArthur: 674 points
Congratulations to House Attenborough on being crowned this year's House Champions!
Thank you to all our pupils and staff for making this year's House Championship such a memorable celebration of teamwork, determination and house pride.
A big thank you to Lilly C-H (Y9), Neev Kainth (Y10) and Lewis Poustie (Y10) from Swan Life Press for the fantastic images taken of our 2026 Sports Day that we've included in this article!

Absence in term time should be avoided.

Unexpected College Closure Information
At Swanmore College, the safety and wellbeing of our pupils and staff is our top priority. In the unlikely event that the College needs to close unexpectedly due to severe weather (such as high winds, flooding or snow), power outages, or other unforeseen circumstances, we will take the following steps to communicate this information effectively:
How we will notify you:
Hampshire County Council Emergency School Closure webpage:
For the latest information on school closures across Hampshire, you can also visit the Hampshire County Council's emergency school closure webpage: https://www.hants.gov.uk/schoolclosures
What to do in case of a closure:
Our commitment to communication:
We understand that unexpected school closures can be disruptive. We are committed to keeping the College community informed as quickly and effectively as possible during such situations.
Please Note:
This information is intended to be a guide, and the specific actions taken in the event of a closure may vary depending on the circumstances.
We appreciate your understanding and cooperation.
